backlog.title: Bug Fix — Auto-Save Integration & Repository Hygiene
backlog.description: End-to-end fix of four issues found during P1 auto-save validation: (1) submitImmediate does not flush per-field numeric debounce saves (Major), (2) committed main HEAD has red test suite + diagnostic probe files (Major), (3) DebouncedFunction.pending() always returns false (Minor), (4) forwardRef render-function warnings in test suite (Minor). The fixes span the debounce adapter code in Form.tsx, the React test suite, and repository hygiene. Architecture findings are stored in plan/004_8583c4771a2e/bugfix/001_e5d9d673f6fd/architecture/system_context.md.

milestones.title: Major Issues — Auto-Save Flush Correctness & Repository Hygiene
milestones.description: Fix the two Major-severity issues: (1) submitImmediate must flush per-field debounce timers, not just the Form-level debouncer; (2) committed main must be green with no diagnostic scratch files, and the isDisabled React limitation must be tracked as a known issue rather than only in skip comments.

tasks.title: Fix submitImmediate to flush per-field debounce timers (Issue 1)
tasks.description: submitImmediate() is the public FormContext API to 'Execute pending debounced submit immediately'. After per-field numeric debounce was added, 'pending debounced submit' includes per-field timers in fieldDebouncersRef. A consumer who edits a per-field-debounced field and calls submitImmediate() must have that save flushed. The fix must flush BOTH form-level and per-field timers as a single coalesced save, avoiding the execution-version-abort race where a trailing timer fires after the flush and bumps executionVersionRef, aborting the flushed save.

subtasks.title: Implement per-field debouncer flush in submitImmediate
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/004_8583c4771a2e/bugfix/001_e5d9d673f6fd/architecture/system_context.md § 'Issue 1' and 'Auto-Save Architecture'. The submitImmediate function is at Form.tsx:722. fieldDebouncersRef is at Form.tsx:225 (Map<number, DebouncedFunction>). pendingChangedFields is at Form.tsx:215 (Set<string>). The PRD's suggested fix (naive forEach flush) is INSUFFICIENT because flushing two timers naively would run executeAutoSave twice — the empty second invocation bumps executionVersionRef and aborts the real first one (dropped save). The correct approach: (a) detect any pending timer via debouncedSubmitRef.current?.pending() || [...fieldDebouncersRef.current.values()].some(fn => fn.pending()), (b) cancel ALL timers (debouncedSubmitRef.current?.cancel() + fieldDebouncersRef.current.forEach(fn => fn.cancel())) so trailing callbacks can't race the flush, (c) run executeAutoSave exactly once via executeAutoSaveRef.current?.(). If no timer is pending, return early (no-op) to avoid a spurious empty save.
2. INPUT: The current submitImmediate at Form.tsx:722-743. The DebouncedFunction interface from types.ts:117-123 (provides cancel/flush/pending). The fieldDebouncersRef at Form.tsx:225. The executeAutoSaveRef ref. Note: this subtask depends on wrapDebounced (Issue 3 fix, P1.M2.T1.S1) being present for pending() to work correctly — BUT submitImmediate can use an alternative detection approach if pending() is still broken. The architecture-correct ordering is: implement wrapDebounced FIRST (P1.M2.T1.S1), then this subtask. However, since the current code already has both fixes, verify the existing implementation matches this contract.
3. LOGIC: Modify submitImmediate in Form.tsx to: (1) check pending state across all debouncers, (2) early-return if nothing pending, (3) cancel all timers, (4) invoke executeAutoSave once. The PRD's repro table: Form-level debounce={3000} + 500ms elapsed → 1 submit after submitImmediate (works today). Per-field inputConfig={{ debounce: 3000 }} + 500ms elapsed → must now be 1 submit (was 0 before fix).
4. OUTPUT: submitImmediate correctly flushes all pending auto-save timers (form-level + per-field) as a single coalesced save. No double-submit, no version-abort race, no spurious empty save when idle.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] The submitImmediate function's inline comment in Form.tsx must explain WHY it cancels-then-invokes rather than naive flushing (to prevent the executionVersionRef race). No README change needed — submitImmediate's public contract ('Execute pending debounced submit immediately') is unchanged; this fix makes the implementation match the documented contract. This rides WITH the work, do not create a separate docs subtask.

subtasks.title: Track the isDisabled React-adapter limitation as a known issue in project documentation
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/004_8583c4771a2e/bugfix/001_e5d9d673f6fd/architecture/system_context.md § 'Issue 2'. The PRD states: 'decide whether the isDisabled React limitation is tracked as a known issue elsewhere (not just in skip comments).' Currently the limitation is ONLY documented in it.skip comments in Field.test.tsx. The root cause is in useFieldDisabledState.ts:126-145 where fieldStates is built without 'disabled' to prevent circular re-render dependencies. The core packages/core/src/conditions/evaluate.ts:84-87 fully supports isDisabled, but the React adapter cannot propagate disabled state into fieldStates without creating infinite re-render loops (field A disabled state depends on field B disabled state which depends on field A...). The potential full fix (optional, not required for this task) would need a non-reactive disabled-state registry that breaks the circular dependency — but that is out of scope for this bugfix.
2. INPUT: The skip comments from P1.M1.T2.S1 documenting the limitation.
3. LOGIC: Create a KNOWN_ISSUES.md file (or add a section to the existing README) at packages/react/KNOWN_ISSUES.md documenting: (a) Title: 'isDisabled field-state condition matcher not functional in React adapter', (b) Symptom: conditions using { isDisabled: true } do not evaluate correctly because fieldStates intentionally omits the disabled property, (c) Root cause: useFieldDisabledState.ts builds fieldStates without disabled to prevent circular re-render dependencies, (d) Workaround: use value-based conditions ({ when: 'source', is: 'disable' }) or explicit disabled props instead of isDisabled, (e) Potential future fix: a non-reactive disabled-state registry, (f) Reference: Field.test.tsx skip comments for specific test cases.
4. OUTPUT: A KNOWN_ISSUES.md file exists at packages/react/KNOWN_ISSUES.md with a clear, actionable description of the limitation. Developers and users can find it without reading test skip comments.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] This subtask IS the documentation — creating KNOWN_ISSUES.md is the deliverable. Update packages/react/README.md to add a 'Known Issues' section linking to KNOWN_ISSUES.md if a README section is warranted.

milestones.title: Minor Issues — Debounce API Correctness & Test Hygiene
milestones.description: Fix the two Minor-severity issues: (3) DebouncedFunction.pending() must reflect the real scheduled state instead of always returning false, and (4) forwardRef render-function warnings in the test suite must be eliminated by replacing unnecessary React.forwardRef() wraps with plain function components.

tasks.title: Fix DebouncedFunction.pending() to track real scheduled state (Issue 3)
tasks.description: Both the Form-level debounced submit and the per-field debounce cache hardcode pending: () => false, violating the DebouncedFunction contract. The lodash debounce fn's .pending() is shadowed by the wrapper's Object.assign. Fix by tracking pending state explicitly in a wrapDebounced helper that sets isPending=true on invocation and clears it on trailing fire/flush/cancel.

subtasks.title: Implement explicit pending() tracking in wrapDebounced helper
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/004_8583c4771a2e/bugfix/001_e5d9d673f6fd/architecture/system_context.md § 'Issue 3' and external_deps.md § 'lodash-es debounce'. The DebouncedFunction interface is at types.ts:117-123. The issue: lodash's debounce DOES expose .pending(), but the project wraps the lodash fn via Object.assign(() => {...}, { cancel, flush, pending }) creating a NEW function object that does NOT share lodash's internal pending state. The fix: create a wrapDebounced(callback, ms) helper function in Form.tsx that: (a) tracks isPending as a closure variable, (b) sets isPending=true when the wrapper function is called, (c) sets isPending=false inside the lodash trailing invocation, inside cancel(), and inside flush(), (d) returns pending: () => isPending. This helper replaces the inline Object.assign in BOTH getOrCreateDebounced (Form.tsx:650) and debouncedSubmit (Form.tsx:689, the normal debounce path only — NOT the immediate adapter where debounce===false). The immediate adapter correctly keeps pending: () => false (an immediate function is never pending).
2. INPUT: The DebouncedFunction interface from types.ts:117-123. The current getOrCreateDebounced at Form.tsx:650-668 and debouncedSubmit useMemo at Form.tsx:689-704. The lodash debounce import.
3. LOGIC: (a) Define wrapDebounced(callback: () => void, ms: number): DebouncedFunction as a module-level function in Form.tsx. It creates a lodash debounce internally, wraps it with an isPending flag, and returns a DebouncedFunction with correct cancel/flush/pending. (b) Update getOrCreateDebounced to use wrapDebounced instead of inline Object.assign. (c) Update the debouncedSubmit useMemo's normal-debounce branch to use wrapDebounced. (d) Leave the immediate adapter (debounce===false) unchanged — its pending: () => false is correct. NOTE: this subtask MUST be done before or alongside P1.M1.T1.S1 because submitImmediate's pending-check depends on wrapDebounced's pending() being correct.
4. OUTPUT: All DebouncedFunction instances (form-level + per-field) report accurate pending state. The immediate adapter correctly reports never-pending. The wrapDebounced helper is reusable and well-documented.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Add a JSDoc comment on wrapDebounced explaining: (1) why lodash's pending is shadowed by Object.assign, (2) the explicit isPending tracking approach, (3) reference to autosave Issue 3. Update the inline comments in getOrCreateDebounced and debouncedSubmit to reference wrapDebounced. This rides WITH the work.

tasks.title: Eliminate forwardRef render-function warnings in the test suite (Issue 4)
tasks.description: The shared test input components used forwardRef<...>(({ value, onChange, name, forwardRef, ... }) => ...) and ignored the second 'ref' parameter, consuming forwardRef from props per the §20 pattern. This triggers React's 'forwardRef render functions accept exactly two parameters' warning. Fix by dropping the unnecessary forwardRef() wrap in test components (the §20 contract delivers forwardRef as a prop) or by accepting the ref parameter.

subtasks.title: Replace forwardRef-wrapped test input components with plain function components
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/004_8583c4771a2e/bugfix/001_e5d9d673f6fd/architecture/system_context.md § 'Issue 4'. The affected test files use shared TestInput/TestSwitch components wrapped in React.forwardRef() but consume forwardRef from props (per §20.4 option A) and ignore the second 'ref' parameter. This triggers: 'Warning: forwardRef render functions accept exactly two parameters: props and ref. Did you forget to use the ref parameter?' The fix: convert these test components from `const TestInput = forwardRef<T, P>(({ value, onChange, forwardRef, ... }) => ...)` to plain function components: `const TestInput = ({ value, onChange, forwardRef, ... }: P & { forwardRef?: React.Ref<T> }) => ...`. The §20 contract delivers the RHF ref as the `forwardRef` prop, so the React.forwardRef() wrap is unnecessary in tests. Files to check and fix: Field.test.tsx (TestInput, TestSwitch), autosave-validation.test.tsx, autosave-field-debounce.test.tsx, autosave-rapid-changes.test.tsx, autosave-async-timing.test.tsx, autosave-submit-immediate.test.tsx, Form.coverage.test.tsx. NOTE: Some test files legitimately use forwardRef<T>((props, ref) => ...) AND wire the ref — those are fine (FormalityProvider.test.tsx, useFormState.test.tsx, priorityOrder.simple.test.tsx, Field.subscriptionStability.test.tsx). Only fix components that IGNORE the ref parameter.
2. INPUT: All test files in packages/react/src/__tests__/ that define input components.
3. LOGIC: For each affected test file: (a) identify the TestInput/TestSwitch component, (b) if it uses React.forwardRef() and ignores the second ref parameter (consuming forwardRef from props instead), convert it to a plain function component with forwardRef as a typed prop, (c) ensure the component still wires ref={forwardRef} on the inner DOM element, (d) add a comment explaining §20.4 option A. (e) Run npx vitest run and verify NO 'forwardRef render functions accept exactly two parameters' warnings appear in stderr.
4. OUTPUT: Zero forwardRef warnings in test output. All test input components that consume forwardRef from props are plain function components. All tests still pass.
5. DOCS: none — no user-facing/config/API surface change. Test-only hygiene fix.
